content:
Apple TV+ currently has a strong lineup of series, including flagship titles such as "Slow Horses" ("Spy Academy"), "Ted Lasso" ("Ted Lasso: Wrong-Goal Star"), and "Dark Matter" ("Dark Matter"), as well as the new comedy "Brothers" starring Matthew McConaughey. In addition, more new works are on the way. Below is all the new content premiering on Apple TV+ in October.

"The Last First: Winter K2" ("The Last First: Winter K2")

  • Release date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

"The Last First: Winter K2," directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells a complex, tense, and moving story that examines the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-changing culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition involving Icelandic climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson and a team made up of Pakistani father and son Ali Sadpara and Sajid Sadpara, whose goal was to become the first team to summit K2 in winter, setting out when the mountain's conditions were at their most severe. The group soon discovered they would be sharing this dangerous journey with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, Nepalese celebrity climber Nims and his Sherpa team. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers into K2's frozen peaks and unpredictable weather, revealing an unexpected, layered story—about strategy and determination, class and social hierarchy, money and power—all playing out in a life-or-death environment.

"The Sisters Grimm" ("The Sisters Grimm") (Season 2)

  • Release date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids and Family

Two orphaned sisters live in a town populated by characters from fantasy stories and fairy tales, facing challenges from heroes and villains while investigating the mystery of their own disappearance from home. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure, offering important lessons for viewers of all ages.

"Small Prophets" ("Small Prophets")

  • Release date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy about eccentric Michael Sleep (played by Pearce Quigley). He has been living an ordinary life since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago—working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (played by Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe with him, with ingredients including rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Michael, holding the recipe, attempts with some skepticism to create homunculi—magical miniature beings that can foresee the future—hoping they can answer the question on his mind: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

"Matchbox The Movie" ("Matchbox The Movie")

  • Release date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

Based on Mattel's iconic toy brand, "Matchbox The Movie" is a thrilling globe-trotting action-adventure film about a group of childhood friends. Their fate is altered when their long-missing former leader, CIA undercover agent Sean (played by John Cena), returns to town, and they are unwittingly drawn into a wild global chase to save the Earth.

"Tenzing" ("Tenzing")

  • Release date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on a true story, recounting the little-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (played by Genden Phuntsok). He was a gifted Himalayan climber who, together with New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (played by Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first people to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (played by Thinley Lhamo), and with the support of expedition secretary Jill Henderson (played by Caitríona Balfe), they convinced Colonel John Hunt (played by Willem Dafoe) to allow Tenzing to be a full member of the British climbing team rather than just a logistics worker. Western climbers saw "Everest" as a goal to conquer, while Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" (Mount Everest) as a sacred mother goddess. The subsequent ascent was tested by tensions in background, class, and individual ambitions, as well as by the dangers of the mountain itself. But at the roof of the world, empire, class, and ambition all gradually faded away, leaving only two outsiders who respected and trusted each other—for Tenzing, this was the moment to fulfill a lifelong dream and spiritual mission.

"Where's Wanda?" ("Where's Wanda?") (Season 2)

  • Release date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple TV+'s first German-language series "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about married couple Dedo and Carlotta Klatt anxiously searching for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda. Wanda disappeared without explanation months ago, and the police have been unable to find her, so the family—with the help of their tech-savvy younger son Ole—gets hold of surveillance equipment and decides to take matters into their own hands. Posing as utility company workers, they install listening devices throughout the neighborhood and half the suburb, only to discover that their neighbors are not what they seem behind closed doors.

"Nocturne" ("Nocturne")

  • Release date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (played by Liev Schreiber). He is a veteran turned murder detective, tired of the hustle and bustle of the Philadelphia streets, so he moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a peaceful life. But when the town and his family are attacked by the cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (played by Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. When an urgent search for Jurek's last missing victim forces Jonah to send his goddaughter—FBI agent Saga Bauer (played by Beetz)—to deal with Jurek, how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers" and more

Apple TV+ will simultaneously air new episodes of several currently airing series in October, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": The comedy series starring Jason Sudeikis will air through October 7
  • "Last Seen": The crime thriller series will air through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy drama will air through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton will air through October 30
  • "Brothers": The comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson will air through November 4

Which of Apple TV+'s October new releases are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, or it can be subscribed to at a discount as part of the Apple One bundle.
